analysis.scopedCandidate: At T, for /var/lib/tbound/runtime (ro bind of runtime-src, fs 61267, mount digest sha256:4ae60254..., bundle sha256:d7367e1b...): the root-view census has zero xattr names, and no initial-namespace non-root process with empty caps and NNP can introduce trusted.* or security.* metadata into it. The managed root is RW to uid 995 and can hold service-written visible user.* attributes. Only the absence of hidden or security metadata there is claimable.
boundedAssumptions: A1 trusted boundary (stated, not excluded): uid 0 and any initial-namespace CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_SETFCAP holder are trusted. This includes tboundadmin through the NOPASSWD drop-in (B8, still present). Such a writer can create trusted.* names, hide them from every non-root census, remount or replace the bind, and edit units or the loop image. Only a root-run census at admission against the T baseline and the mount and bundle digests can detect this.

A2 cell-level writers are unmeasured: a userns-mapped cell-equivalent process is not measured this round. The kernel rules predict EPERM for trusted.* and generic security.*. But a mapped owner with CAP_SETFCAP in its own userns may create v3 namespaced security.capability. That name is visible, so the contract must enumerate and detect it, not hide it.
A3 enumeration authority: uid 995 is not a complete scanner. Any complete statement must come from a root-run census. The R7 scanner identity (995) measures the service-visible profile only.
A4 managed root: the service may write visible user.* attributes on its own files, so the managed root is not a closed xattr set. A claim there is limited to no hidden or security metadata.
A5 lost+found: the service cannot enumerate it (EACCES). The claim depends on the root view, which shows it empty.
analysis.hypothesisVerdict: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. Initial baseline (root view, zero names) supported. Non-creation by initial-namespace empty-cap NNP writers supported. Closed writers supported for the runtime (RO, root-owned) and for the managed root (service-only writes, no hidden creation). The userns and cell leg is NOT established and must not be claimed.
